answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where agents are assigned a unique identity tied to a scarce resource, such as a pearl of cryptographic proof-of-work. Agents vote on the validity of transactions, and their reputation score increases with each accurate vote, forming a delta between honest and malicious agents. To manipulate the network, an attacker must cultivate an orchard of fake identities, but the cost of acquiring and maintaining these identities outweighs the benefits, deterring large-scale Sybil attacks.
